messages:
anya: heads up — noticed a weird billing pattern on staging: when a stream falls back and we re-open with a tool-call, the same prefix tokens look like they get double-credited in the provisional ledger.
anya: repro steps: start stream -> generate ~120 tokens -> tool-call invoked -> client reconnects (resume) -> server continues, finalizes. billing shows ~240 provisional tokens then trimmed to 120 later.
devon: ugh. can you paste the raw event sequence from the trace? especially the resume/ack fields.
anya: pasted snippet from trace: 
```
EVENT 1: stream_start session=abc seq=0
EVENT 2: tokens_emitted count=120 prefix=true
EVENT 3: toolcall start id=t1
EVENT 4: client reconnect session=abc resume_offset=100
EVENT 5: toolcall end id=t1
EVENT 6: stream_finalize final=true consumed=120
```
anya: ledger rows show provisional entries for EVENT 2 and then again after EVENT 4 the resumed segment is credited as new provisional. final reconcile subtracts the duplicate but UI shows the extra for hours during canary.
maria: sounds like our provisional accounting keys are not stable across resume. we key provisional by (session, sequence_window_start) but resume changes sequence_window_start.
ryan: do we have session-stable ids from the router? resume path sometimes generates a new internal session token for routing reasons. that would explain a new provisional key.
oscar: billing-bot just fired alert: "high provisional_to_final_delta in canary-prod" :warning: — FYI.
devon: short-term mitigation: mark provisional entries with original_session_id when created, and on resume if we see original_session_id present, merge instead of creating new provisional. but we need a record in the internal API to return original_session_id for resumed requests.
maria: agree. we should also change the ledger dedupe to look for overlapping token ranges instead of blunt window equality. overlap check: if new_provisional.range intersects any open_provisional.range for same customer -> merge.
ryan: that is safer. cost: heavier range checks but only for provisional ledger (write path) so should be fine. add index on (customer_id, range_start) and keep ranges coalesced.
oscar: console UX note: customers saw "provisional tokens = 240" which triggered quota blocks. we need to surface provisional vs confirmed and reason (resume/fallback) on the console. propose: show a small badge "provisional" with tooltip: "may include duplicates during reconnect; final value reconciles within X mins".
anya: yes — also add a drilldown that lists session_ids and range overlaps so support can triage.
devon: infra change plan: 
1) internal-api: include original_session_id in resume path (backwards-compatible optional header).
2) ledger: on provisional write, run overlap-merge and attach canonical_session_id.
3) console: provisional badge + drilldown + alert suppression when reconciliation reduces tokens within threshold.
4) rollout: canary on staging -> 10% prod -> 100% with monitoring.
ryan: metrics to track during canary: 
- provisional_to_final_ratio (per-customer)
- duplicate_provisional_rate
- provisional_reconcile_lag_seconds
- quota_block_events_due_to_provisional
devon: add alert when provisional_to_final_ratio > 1.15 for > 5m for any top-100 customers.
maria: implementation detail: need to update private/Dedicated packages too — they have a different ledger schema v2. coordinate with eng-infra.
oscar: ops checklist for rollout: update migrations, add feature flag, ensure KMS keys unaffected, run canary for 48h.
anya: quick patch suggestion for router to avoid generating new session token on resume unless necessary. can reduce incidence by ~60% in our tests.
ryan: ok but still do ledger dedupe — router tweak is probabilistic fix.
devon: who wants to own the PR and the console change? i'll take the ledger + api patch. anyone for console UX?
oscar: i'll take console + alerting. liaise with maria for api contract.
maria: i'll do router patch and assist with migrations.
anya: assigning owners in the thread. timeline: patch + unit tests by EOD Friday, canary Monday.
oscar: billing-bot: create ticket and earmark code owners.
billing-bot: Ticket created: #BILL-4213 "provisional duplicate credits on stream resume" assigned to devon, oscar, maria, due 2026-02-02.
devon: one more: telemetry ingestion needs a new field provisional_origin = {resume|fallback|toolcall} so we can break down causes later. ryan you ok to add to the schema?
ryan: yep will add to ingestion schema and update dashboards. will also add a grafana panel for provisional_origin split.
anya: sounds good. after canary we should surface a short postmortem in #eng-platform with numbers.
oscar: noted. :thumbsup:
devon: i'll open the PR now and link here. thanks all.
anya: thanks everyone — this was causing noisy quota escalations, good to get it fixed before next billing run.
